title: The judgment type, the dismissal, the appeal window and the enforcement task have no column, no list value and no owned row, and the delivery that opens them has no source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-016, its Acceptance criteria, Data, Endpoints and Screen and states tables); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T4, appendix T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.16.2, A2.16.3.1, A2.16.3.3); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-44, R-LIT-45, R-LIT-46, R-LIT-51); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-LIT-16, FEAT-LIT-20); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4, two tables and five REST operations)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3, 6, 7, 8, 9; s8 BR4, BR5, BR6, BR7; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.5; s12.6; s12.7; s13 Solution plan; s14; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC5 and AC6, s11 Data, s12.5, s12.6, s12.7, s13, s19
description: Both slices of RWB-E5-016 record a judgment that the sources describe with more facts than the data model holds. legal_action carries judgment_date (DF-LEG-011), judgment_amount (DF-LEG-012) and red_case_no (DF-LEG-007), but it carries no judgment_type, no dismissal flag and no appeal-window end, and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS is OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED and WITHDRAWN with no dismissed value and no appeal value. The two rules need judgment_type in (full, partial, default) and judgment_type = dismissed, and R-LIT-45 needs an appeal window that R-LIT-46 tests with appeal_window_ends is in the future, so the type and the window are carried as inputs of the PATCH operation and as facts of the decision record, and the appeal window is held as one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow whose end is a reference value. The enforcement task that R-LIT-44 opens is a task row, which is P3 rwb-case's table (DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026) and not this service's, so it is requested on the case-move answer and created by rwb-case. The decision log entry of the legacy Data table is decision_log_entry in rwb_decision (P7) and is written here through the local decision-record library of DP-03, never as a row of that table. No source names the operation by which rwb-case creates the task or answers the move, and no source gives the appeal window end or the full judgment-type vocabulary beyond the four words of the two rules.
evidence: TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines legal_action with DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and no judgment_type, no dismissal and no appeal-window field, while DF-LEG-011 judgment_date and DF-LEG-012 judgment_amount are the only judgment facts; T3.2 gives LOV-LEGAL-STATUS as OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN; T4 gives R-LIT-44 IN_HEARING to JUDGMENT_RECORDED and R-LIT-45 IN_HEARING to JUDGMENT_DISMISSED; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-44 and R-LIT-45 carry the conditions judgment_type in (full, partial, default) and judgment_type = dismissed with the 5 working days and to the appeal window end timers, and R-LIT-46 tests appeal_window_ends is in the future with no field of that name in the data model; FSD S4 A2.16.3.1 gives the same two rules and no field list; the context pack lists two tables, hearing and legal_action, and one workflow; the legacy Data table names recovery_case, task, decision_log_entry and rule_row, of which only the legal action facts are this service's.
area: Data model and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P3 rwb-case owner and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: Keep the metadata and data rows as the plan gives them, record the judgment date, the amount and the red case number on legal_action, carry the judgment type and the dismissal as inputs and record facts, hold the appeal window as one durable timer with a reference value, and let step D1 decide whether a judgment-type column or an appeal-window field is added by the DB story of this service.

title: The trigger of the step, the v_ace_lawsuit read of the feature extract and the three consumed owner contracts have no single source, and no contract row is planned
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4, five REST operations and no view; naming and shared platform rules); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-LIT-16, the v_ace_lawsuit read and runs unattended); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.16.2, A2.16.3.3, A2.16.4.4); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T2, T5.1, T5.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-016, its Story paragraph and permission table); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E5-016, the C, I and X lists)
section: APP s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 1; s10 Authority; s12.2; s12.4; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19; CON s2, s3, s7 AC3 and AC4, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.8, s13
description: The step has no single stated trigger. The legacy story's AC1 says Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place and When its trigger arrives, the FSD S4 A2.16.2 names the trigger as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer and A2.16.4.4 declares no background event, TSD S4 T5.3 declares no event, and the FSD A2.16.3.3 says the step runs unattended while the legacy story names an enforcement owner who records the judgment and the permission table gives the litigation right to RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, PT-LAWFIRM and SY-DATALOAD. Both stories therefore read the judgment as a signal of LitigationWorkflow forwarded at IN_HEARING, entered by the firm on the partner portal or arriving on the LIT interface, and declare no event and no Schedule. The feature extract of the thin story adds a fact the architecture does not give this service: it writes the judgment from the firm or the LIT lawsuit read through v_ace_lawsuit. The context pack gives S4 two tables, five REST operations and no view, and the architecture keeps the recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data, so the view is declared as a prohibition and the judgment reaches legal_action on the LIT interface (INT-09). The three consumed reads — the case read, the case-move answer with the enforcement task request and the rule package read — are C dependencies in fact while both metadata rows carry None, so the stories build against the published documents and the fakes. The activity names recordJudgment and armAppealWindow, the judgment element of the PATCH payload, the task-request element and the decision code are design names with no source.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.16.2 step 1 gives Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and A2.16.4.4 is the row None, No background event; A2.16.3.3 gives None; runs unattended as primary with the enforcement owner as also-user; the legacy story AC1 says its trigger arrives and its permission table gives Litigation U to RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, PT-LAWFIRM and SY-DATALOAD and Litigation C to RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-16 reads Writes the judgment date and amount onto the case, from the firm or the LIT lawsuit read through v_ace_lawsuit, and runs unattended; TSD S4 v2 T5.1 gives INT-09 LIT as a daily COLLINS batch and T5.3 gives no event; T-A.2 gives PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId} as the operation that records a filing, judgment or enforcement step and no operation of rwb-case or rwb-decision; the context pack lists two tables, hearing and legal_action, five REST operations and zero events, and its naming rules say ACE data only through the owner contract or the v_ace_* views, which this service does not hold; the plan rows of RWB-S4-E5016-APP and RWB-S4-E5016-CON carry C, I and X as empty lists.
area: Workflow, integration and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case, P7 rwb-decision, P2 rwb-integration and P1 rwb-source-data
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the solution architect and the P2 rwb-integration owner
proposed: Start the step from the judgment signal the parent workflow forwards on task queue rwb-litigation, publish the judgment element and the task request in the baseline review, declare the v_ace_lawsuit read as a prohibition and let step D1 decide whether the three consumed rows become C dependencies of this key.

title: The legacy key carries no requirement id in the story master and the plan carries no requirement for either slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-016, its metadata table with no Requirement row); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (the reqs list of both slices, empty); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (Requirements served, REQ-S4-007); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T8)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s18 Traceability
description: The traceability of the two stories needs one sourced requirement. The legacy story master of RWB-E5-016 carries no requirement id, the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, and TSD S4 T8 names no requirement for the judgment feature. The only requirement of the module that names the outcome of the step is REQ-S4-007, Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement, which is exactly what AC1 asks by opening the enforcement step for RW-ENFORCE, so both stories trace to it and the empty plan list is recorded rather than filled with an invented identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-016 gives Epic, Module, Feature, Process, Priority, Depends on and Decision only; the plan rows of RWB-S4-E5016-APP and RWB-S4-E5016-CON carry reqs as an empty list; FSD S4 Requirements served gives REQ-S4-007 Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement; TSD S4 T8 lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 against FEAT-LIT-01 only, with Written one epic ahead in the story column.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both slices to REQ-S4-007 and let step D1 update the plan reqs list of the two slices to that identifier.

title: The FSD S4 and the TSD S4 that the two slices read are In review with an empty sign-off table and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (status); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3 Preconditions; CON s3 Preconditions
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S4 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table and the TSD S4 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, and the run of D-RCV-60 has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.
evidence: FSD S4 document control gives Status In review and its document sign-off table has empty Name, Signature and Date cells; TSD S4 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status changes.
